- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for the next 3–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the next 5–10 days.
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting back to 60–65 after 70+), check sentiment for reversal signals — if sentiment shifts to neutral or positive, allow slight upward correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price increases (especially after sentiment turns positive); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.
